run.change_description:
commit-ec0e33b3: Avoid setting a connection's `ca_certs` or `ca_cert_dir` attributes when `verify=True`

commit-8f954567: Use a default SSLContext with the default CA bundle loaded when `verify=True`

commit-f21e70bf: Rename default SSLContext to make it private by convention

commit-4089f3dc: Wrap line to comply with CI lint

summary.intent: Avoid a per-request urllib3 load_verify_locations() call (a known, measurably slow OpenSSL FFI call) when verify=True, by preloading the default CA bundle into one module-level SSLContext at import time and handing that same context to every verify=True connection pool, instead of letting each pool trigger its own load.
summary.issue_fit: No linked issue; intent taken from the supplied PR body (spec-pr-psf-requests-6667) and the four real commit messages. The stated goal (skip redundant load_verify_locations() calls for verify=True while leaving verify=True/False and client-cert behavior otherwise unchanged) is partially met: the caching works for the common case, but the preserved-behavior premise fails for verify=True combined with a client certificate (see finding).
summary.coverage: Full merge-base diff reviewed (src/requests/adapters.py, the only changed file, +28/-18, single complete chunk). Traced pool_kwargs construction through the installed urllib3==2.8.0 dependency's connection pooling, connection, and ssl_ modules to establish how `ssl_context`, `cert_file`/`key_file`, and `ca_certs`/`ca_cert_dir` pool kwargs are consumed. No tests were added or changed by this diff, so nothing was owed under changed-test inspection; existing cert/verify/mTLS tests were run once at head as a sanity check (see check_details).
check_details: Caller-supplied context: two tests are known to fail at both base and head due to an environment/fixture cert mismatch ('Missing Authority Key Identifier') unrelated to this diff: tests/test_requests.py::test_pyopenssl_redirect and ::test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert. Accepted as historical/environmental, not evaluated further.

Reviewer ran `PYTHONPATH=<clone>/src <cache>/venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_requests.py -k "tls_settings or mtls_settings"` at head 4089f3dc: 2 passed, 2 failed. One failure is the caller-named test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert. The other, test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings, was not named by the caller; it fails inside the test's first call (`verify=False`), whose connection-pool configuration is byte-identical between base and head (the `verify is False` branch of `_urllib3_request_context()` is unchanged by this diff), so this failure is the same pre-existing environment/cert-fixture mismatch class, not introduced by this change.

Reviewer wrote and ran a focused scratch test (test_ssl_context_leak.py, outside the clone) at head 4089f3dc to fact-check the confirmed finding below: 2 passed, reproducing that requests.adapters._preloaded_ssl_context is the identical object handed to every verify=True pool regardless of client_cert, and that loading a client certificate onto it (as urllib3 does whenever cert_file is set) makes an unrelated, cert-less verify=True connection subsequently offer that certificate, while a same-built-but-unmutated control context does not.

findings.title: Don't load a per-request client certificate onto the shared, process-wide SSL context
findings.trigger: Any call anywhere in the process of `session.request(..., cert=(certfile, keyfile))` (or `cert=certfile`) with the default `verify=True`, together with any other `verify=True` request to a different host that does not itself pass `cert=`.
findings.impact: `_urllib3_request_context()` hands out the single module-level `_preloaded_ssl_context` to every verify=True pool, cert or not. urllib3 calls `context.load_cert_chain(certfile, keyfile)` on whatever `ssl_context` it's given whenever `cert_file` is set, so one client-cert request permanently loads that certificate onto the shared object; every other verify=True connection in the process, to any host, then silently presents it too - a cross-host client-certificate leak, confirmed by a focused reproduction (fresh handshake with the shared context offers the cert; a same-built control context does not).
findings.change: In `_urllib3_request_context()`, stop reusing `pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context` whenever `client_cert` is also set; build (or cache per client-cert-pair) a fresh SSLContext for that case instead, so a client certificate never gets loaded onto the shared default context.
findings.source: PR conversation (non-review-comment-5, tiran, 2024-05-05T05:08:40Z): "[SSLContext] is thread safe as long as you don't reconfigure it once it is used by a connection... changing... mTLS certs can lead to surprising behavior."

observations.fact: `_preloaded_ssl_context.load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH))` now runs unconditionally at `requests.adapters` import time, whereas before this change the equivalent CA-bundle resolution only ran lazily, inside `cert_verify()`, the first time an HTTPS request with `verify=True` was actually made.
